candidates.potentialGuestroomDemand: Delegate, speaker, VIP or overflow lodging; peak rooms not published.
candidates.evidenceOfHospitalityDemand: Official event page describes a multi-day conference and tradeshow for utility leaders and industry partners; confirmed competing hotel is a constraint, so pursue only overflow/future edition intelligence.
candidates.knownCompetitiveConstraints: Venue is committed elsewhere; do not treat venue inventory as hotel opportunity.
suggestedDeepResearchQuestions: Confirm expected out-of-town participation and any official housing or hotel RFP.
Identify the event owner, housing/meeting lead and sourcing deadline.
candidates.suggestedRelationshipDevelopmentAction: Contact the organizer or institutional events function to introduce the hotel for delegate lodging, side meetings and overflow consideration; do not claim availability.

structured.rankingRationale: Top-ranked opportunities combine exact future dates, a named organizer and a central Toronto venue with a plausible delegate, executive or speaker lodging mechanism. Exploration 27 ranks highest for current accessibility because hotel negotiations are explicitly underway; Future of Work, Law & Freedom, CBA and EDIST are discounted or routed to constraint/monitoring because a venue or hotel commitment is already published. Small campus events remain useful but require attendance and travel-origin verification.

rejectedOrFlagged.label: Generic Toronto incentive-travel marketing pages
rejectedOrFlagged.reason: They describe possible programmes or packages, not a verified future organized trip with a named company, date and venue.

rejectedOrFlagged.label: Toronto Congress Centre / airport-area events
rejectedOrFlagged.reason: Outside the supplied Harbourfront/downtown/MTCC/Exhibition Place/university-hospital territory or lacked a specific accessible hotel mechanism.

notesForDeepResearch: Verify whether any event has a housing agency, official hotel list or open RFP before outreach.
Prioritize Exploration 27 because its official page explicitly says hotel preferred-rate negotiations are underway.
Treat confirmed venue and hotel blocks as constraints, not as Radisson inventory.
For small university events, test delegate geography and speaker travel before estimating commercial value.
materialUncertainties: Most candidates do not publish attendance, peak rooms, hotel RFP status or contracting authority.
The hotel’s restaurant/lounge and current catering operating status require separate verification.
No qualifying future incentive/recognition trip with a named non-hotel organizer, exact Toronto dates and venue was verified in this pass; do not infer one from generic incentive marketing.

result.text: 15 Toronto event-driven opportunities were identified for the 18-month window. The set emphasizes exact future dates, named organizers, specific downtown or campus venues, and explicit or plausible lodging/meeting mechanisms. Confirmed competing venues are flagged as constrained rather than treated as open inventory; unsupported attendance and room blocks remain null.
